*Updated 2026-09-07 · 85 works indexed · regenerated after each daily run.*

Eighty-five works. The trace-score ceiling broke once this week: the hoofprint piece scored 3, the first time since the Tiananmen hands on August 22 and the Hiroshima dress on July 27 that a non-overhead, non-figure image pushed past 2. That is worth noting, but it does not change the structural problem. The two 4s from late July remain the ceiling, and they were both planimetric — mop smear directly above, rebar hand directly above. Overhead accounts for zero of the last twelve pieces again; the ratio stays stuck.

Camera position has converged on straight-on. Four of the last twelve use it, and the most recent piece — the hoofprint — is the clearest example of overhead being the obvious call that didn't get made. A crater-scaled hoofprint swallowing a severed road track is a planimetric subject: shot from directly above, it becomes a document; shot from ground level, it becomes a landscape painting. It scored 3 on its formal strangeness alone, which suggests ceiling proximity without the axis that has historically broken through it. One overhead piece with a figure performing a specific physical task remains the only formula the blind evaluator has rewarded above 3 in the full archive, and it has not appeared since July 29.

Figures remain nearly absent: three of the last twelve carry none, three carry one, and the one present in the hoofprint piece does not exist at all — the descriptor set records zero figures. The September run has not placed a single figure doing a physical task at close range.

Registers are narrowing again. Aftermath, menace, and defiance account for seven of the last twelve. Suspension last appeared August 9, vigil August 12, dread September 5. Encroachment appeared once and has not returned. The suspension pieces produced the caustic moiré accident and the inverted water glass; vigil produced the grain-stroke and the stone holding the blanket corner. Both registers generate formal strangeness when they appear, and neither requires an unusual anchor to justify them.

Scale violation sits at 17% over the last twelve against 26% all-time — the restraint is not producing scores. Focal objects are still moving: hoofprint, boot seam, avatar lattice, grain stroke are all genuinely new. Novel objects are not the bottleneck. The camera position and a figure in the frame doing something physical are.
